subject: Post-call: Throughput playbook & token-rate signal mapping
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Ruth Chang <ruth.chang@ledgerly.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Throughput playbook & token-rate signal mapping

Hi Ruth — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our side so the Ledgerly engineering team can validate SLO readiness for the pilot. Short version up top, details below.

Key asks / agreement items:
- Target 95th pctl latency SLO: 300ms for short-chat endpoints (<=128 tokens).
- Peak window: 9:30–10:15 PDT daily, expected 2.8k QPS at burst; steady-state baseline outside peak ~320 QPS.
- Token-rate signal: typical message size ~120 tokens, median 78 tokens, peak 1.2k tokens (rare).
- Streaming: some flows require server-sent token streaming for partial responses; target 95th pctl streaming start-time <= 150ms.

What we captured from the call (workload characterization):
- Most traffic is conversational assistant (80%) with short prompts and 1–2-shot context.
- 10% of calls are long-form summarization (>>512 tokens) that will be routed to a separate batch model.
- Concurrency per session estimated 1.2 requests/sec on average; client-side multiplexing may cause micro-bursts of concurrent connections.

Immediate next steps we propose:
1) You share a 48-hour sampled export (attachment) of request-level data (timestamps, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_hint) — we received ledgerly_workload_snapshot_Jun30.csv.
2) Redwood will run an initial mapping: tokens/sec -> qps -> GPU slots and return two options (latency-optimized and cost-optimized). Target delivery: 3 business days.
3) Quick sync next week to align rollout: can you confirm preferred times?

If anything above is off, call it out and we'll correct. Attaching the copy of the notes and the recording.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0134

Attachments: ledgerly_workload_snapshot_Jun30.csv; call-recording-20270630.mp3
From: Ruth Chang <ruth.chang@ledgerly.com>

Cc: Ledgerly Platform Team <platform@ledgerly.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Throughput playbook & token-rate signal mapping

Thanks Jonas — this matches our notes. A couple clarifications from the Ledgerly side:
- The 2.8k QPS burst is for a 15-minute marketing notification window; sustained peak is usually 6–8 minutes inside that window.
- Median prompt size is closer to 65 tokens if you exclude auto-generated system prompts (they added noise in our earlier export). I attached a cleaned CSV to the Drive folder.
- For streaming: clients expect partial results for the top-k tokens; if the first TCP chunk takes >200ms we're seeing user drop-off. So 150ms is great, but 200ms is the hard cutoff.

Next: we'll grant Redwood read-only access to the sampling folder on GDrive and confirm a time next Tuesday (13:00–15:00 PDT) for a validation session with our infra team (Tom & Priya).

Ruth Chang
Head of Platform Engineering | Ledgerly
ruth.chang@ledgerly.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Throughput playbook & token-rate signal mapping

Marissa / Sean / Karthik — forwarding Ruth's clarifications. Highlights for ops/input:
- Burst windows are shorter (6–8m inside the 15m window); adjust burst headroom calculations accordingly.
- Median tokens ~65 after cleanup; workload CSV in Drive.
- Streaming hard cutoff 200ms (user drop-off); initial SLO target 150ms 95th pctl.

Can you please run a quick what-if using the sample (ledgerly_workload_snapshot_Jun30.csv) and return:
A) Estimated GPUs and concurrency needed for latency-optimized config (95th <=300ms, streaming start <=150ms).
B) Estimated GPUs and concurrency for cost-optimized config (95th <=350ms, streaming <=200ms).
C) Any hot-spot concerns (KV cache miss amplification, prefix-heavy prompts).

Deliverable: concise table + recommended rollout (canary percent, fallback model) by Tue EOD (5 Jul).

Thanks — I'll loop Ruth back once we have numbers.
Jonas
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: Throughput playbook & token-rate signal mapping

Quick internal runbook notes — findings from initial sizing pass: (attachment: sla-draft-Ledgerly-2027-07.pdf)

Summary: with cleaned median 65 tokens and the burst profile (2.8k QPS peak for 6–8m), we see two viable configurations:
- Latency-optimized (prod): ~12 x A100s (40GB) behind a multi-model pool with prefix cache enabled; steady baseline capacity: 2 x A100s; canary 5% -> 25% over 24h. This configuration targets 95th pctl <=300ms and streaming-start <=150ms for <=128 token requests.
- Cost-optimized (pilot): ~6 x A100s reserved, autoscale burst to 10x with pre-warmed slots for expected 8-min bursts. Targets 95th pctl <=350ms and streaming <=200ms.

Operational asks / risks:
- KV cache: we recommend a prefix-key eviction TTL of 30 minutes for Ledgerly's chat patterns to reduce cache churn.
- Long-form summarization should be routed to batch nodes with longer token budgets to avoid tail impact on short-chat SLOs.
- Network egress at peak may require higher pNIC tuning; flagging to infra.

Next steps we're proposing:
1) Share the sizing slides with Ledgerly and get approval on pilot vs prod config.
2) Prep a canary plan: 100 users -> 1k QPS staged increments; test streaming latency under synthetic replay.
3) Contract note: include a soft SLA ramp for first 30 days while cache warms — we'll tie credits to missed pcts.

I'll attach the draft SLA and numbers. Sean, can you run a short synthetic replay script (5m) with token-size distribution and confirm streaming start-time on our staging cluster? Karthik, please sanity-check the burst autoscale times we modeled (we used 30s warm-up per GPU).

Marissa Cole
Manager, Performance Solutions | Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: Throughput playbook & token-rate signal mapping

Quick status: ran the 5-minute synthetic with the Ledgerly token distribution on staging (attached logs to the Drive link). Results: streaming-start median 82ms, 95th 138ms under 1k QPS target. Under a 2.8k synthetic burst we saw 95th ~310ms on staging (no cache warmed, single AZ). With prefix cache warm and multi-AZ routing we expect to hit the latency-optimized numbers Jonas requested.

I'll coordinate the replay window with Ledgerly for Tue 13:00–14:00 PDT and share the exact script.

Sean Gallagher
Perf Engineer | Redwood Inference
